summary: Policy night for Craze & Crash: no new YouTube rule affects us (the July renaming to 'generic or repetitive content' and the May AI labels; we use real licensed footage and no AI scenes). Added 4 sourced Short topics: Dollar Shave Club, Microsoft and Nokia, Yahoo's refused $44.6B, and the Crocs crash.
why: Founder bet, the core Short format, had one open topic; now three. References: Nokia 2.7M on a 20.7K channel, Crocs 777K on 3.65K, Gillette and Dollar Shave Club 653K on 10.8K, Yahoo 64.8K on 19.3K. Our two public Shorts have no stayed-to-watch data yet, so no proposal from our own numbers.

findings.title: Nokia's fall is this month's biggest niche Short
findings.detail: 2.7M views on a 20.7K channel (14 s) and 6.0M on a 281K channel. Topic added: Microsoft paid EUR 5.44B, then wrote off $7.6B.

findings.title: YouTube's 'inauthentic content' is now 'generic or repetitive content'
findings.detail: A renaming, no new rule (16 Jul 2026). Our risk would be a narrated stock-footage compilation; the profile and recipe already forbid it.

findings.title: AI labels are now prominent and applied automatically
findings.detail: Only for photorealistic AI-made content; we use real licensed photos and footage, so containsSyntheticMedia stays false.

findings.title: Dollar Shave Club: a ~$4,500 video to a reported $1B sale
findings.detail: Revenue $4M, $19M, $65M in 2012-14 (founder, Fortune). A core founder-bet Short.
